name: Traceability Matrix - SVM
rows: Service governance, portfolio, value and performance
Develop, establish and implement security monitoring arrangements to identify the effectiveness of the entity's security plan and establish a continuous cycle of improvement.
ITSM must provide measurable monitoring, service review and continual-improvement evidence for the security plan and service effectiveness.
High - direct ITSM governance, observability and metrics requirement.
Service strategy, monitoring, observability and customer experience metrics

The ICT Service Management Policy must require service monitoring, trend analysis, service reviews and improvement actions that evidence service effectiveness, security control performance and customer impact.
Incident, problem, breach, cyber extortion and statutory reporting
Procedures are developed, implemented and maintained to ensure security incidents are responded to and managed.
Incident and major incident processes are the ITSM mechanism for identifying, triaging, escalating and resolving security-related disruptions.
High - directly applicable to incident and major incident management.
Incident management and major incident management

The policy must require security incidents or suspected security incidents raised through service desk, monitoring or supplier channels to be logged, prioritised, escalated to Security/CISO and managed through agreed incident and major incident procedures.
Service continuity, backup, resilience, critical services and emergency integration
Security incident management and response plans are incorporated into the entity's business continuity arrangements.
Security incident response must be integrated with continuity and DR so service restoration aligns with business continuity priorities.
High - direct interface between incident management, service continuity and DR.
Service continuity and disaster recovery interface

The policy must require major incident and security incident plans to align with business continuity, disaster recovery, communication and service restoration arrangements, including RTO/RPO and escalation obligations.
Incident, problem, breach, cyber extortion and statutory reporting
Significant or externally reportable security incidents and referral obligations are reported to the relevant authority (or authorities) within the applicable timeframe.
Major incident procedures need defined thresholds, timeframes and owners for regulator, ASD, Home Affairs or other external reporting.
High - direct major incident escalation and reporting requirement.

The policy must require significant or externally reportable ICT/security incidents to be escalated immediately to accountable business, Security, Legal/Privacy and communications owners for reporting within mandated timeframes.
Incident, problem, breach, cyber extortion and statutory reporting
Procedures are developed, implemented and maintained to investigate security incidents in accordance with the principles of the Australian Government Investigations Standards.
Post-incident investigation outputs feed problem management, root cause analysis, lessons learned and control improvement.
Medium - ITSM supports evidence and corrective actions; Security owns investigations.

The policy must require incident records, evidence preservation, post-incident reviews and problem records to support security investigations, root-cause analysis and agreed corrective actions without compromising investigation integrity.
Risk management, assurance, internal control and fraud prevention
The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
Service risk acceptance and change risk decisions must align with the entity's documented security risk tolerance.
Medium - governance interface with enterprise/security risk management.
Service strategy, governance and risk alignment

The policy must require service owners and ITSM process owners to align service design, change, release, continuity and supplier decisions with approved security risk tolerance and accepted residual risk.
Risk management, assurance, internal control and fraud prevention
A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
ITSM needs named owners for service, supplier, change, configuration and continuity risks, including shared risks.
Medium - supports clear accountability across service management processes.

The policy must assign accountable service owners, process owners and risk owners/stewards for ICT services and shared service risks, with escalation to Security and enterprise risk owners where required.
Risk management, assurance, internal control and fraud prevention
The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
ICT service decisions can affect other entities, suppliers and participants; ITSM must manage cross-entity risk communication.
Medium - applies to changes, incidents, releases and shared services.
Change enablement, release management and stakeholder communications

The policy must require material service changes, incidents and risk decisions to consider impacts on other entities and suppliers, and to share relevant risk information through agreed governance and communication channels.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance

The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
Supplier and outsourced service risks directly affect ICT service outcomes and underpinning contracts.
High - direct supplier management and UC requirement.

The policy must require ICT service procurement, onboarding and contract management to identify security and service risks before engagement and maintain risk ownership throughout the supplier lifecycle.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance

Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
ITSM supplier contracts must include PSPF-aligned service, security, incident, continuity and reporting obligations.
High - direct UC/OLA/SLA and supplier policy requirement.
Supplier management, OLAs, UCs and SLAs

The policy must require ICT contracts, OLAs and UCs to include proportionate security, availability, incident reporting, continuity, change, data handling and audit obligations before operational acceptance.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
Supplier compliance with relevant PSPF controls must be monitored as part of service performance and governance.

The policy must require suppliers, contractors and subcontractors supporting ICT services to comply with applicable security and service management obligations and provide evidence through service reviews, audits and assurance activities.
Incident, problem, breach, cyber extortion and statutory reporting

Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
Actual or suspected supplier security incidents must enter NDIA incident and major incident workflows quickly.
High - direct supplier incident escalation requirement.

The policy must require supplier contracts and operating procedures to mandate prompt notification of actual or suspected security incidents, cooperation with investigations and compliance with NDIA direction during incident response.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
IRAP reports and assurance artefacts support service acceptance and supplier risk management for outsourced services.
Medium - applies when NDIA consumes government outsourced or cloud services.
Service design, transition and supplier assurance
The policy must require relevant IRAP assessments and supplier assurance artefacts to be obtained, reviewed and recorded before service acceptance and during periodic service reviews.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance

Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
Contractual controls must be monitored over the service lifecycle, not only at onboarding.
High - direct supplier performance and continual assurance requirement.
Supplier management and service level management

The policy must require ongoing review of supplier security controls, service levels, subcontractor obligations and corrective actions through governance forums, SLA/UC reviews and risk-based assurance.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
Service exit, transition and termination controls are needed to protect data, knowledge, assets, access and continuity.
High - direct service transition/supplier exit requirement.
Service transition, supplier exit and knowledge management
The policy must require service exit and termination plans covering access removal, data return or disposal, knowledge transfer, configuration updates, continuity risks and residual obligations.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
Foreign ownership, control or influence risks may affect critical ICT suppliers and service continuity.
Medium - supplier due diligence interface; procurement/security own detailed assessment.
Supplier risk management and service strategy

The policy must require supplier selection and service review processes to consider security risk due diligence, including ownership/control changes, and escalate material risks through procurement and Security governance.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
Supplier risks evolve during operations; ITSM must reassess them through service reviews, changes and incidents.
High - direct supplier lifecycle risk requirement.
Supplier management and continual service improvement
The policy must require supplier and contract risks to be reviewed after material changes, incidents, performance failures and periodic service reviews, with actions tracked to closure.
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance
Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
The ITSM policy must prefer trusted suppliers and ensure exceptions are risk accepted by the right security authority.
Supplier management, service design and risk acceptance
The policy must require ICT services to use secure and verifiable suppliers and platforms unless a documented business need and CISO-approved residual risk acceptance support an exception.
Service continuity, backup, resilience, critical services and emergency integration
A business continuity plan is developed, implemented and maintained to respond effectively and minimise the impacts of significant business disruptions to the entity's critical services and assets.
Service continuity is a core ITSM capability for sustaining critical ICT services and supporting business continuity.
Service continuity and disaster recovery interface

The policy must require critical ICT services to have service continuity arrangements aligned to business continuity plans, including restoration priorities, dependencies, RTO/RPO, testing and improvement actions.
Service continuity, backup, resilience, critical services and emergency integration
Plans for managing a broad range of emergencies are integrated within the business continuity plan.
Emergency and disruption plans must integrate with service desk, major incident, communications and DR playbooks.
Medium - ITSM interface with enterprise emergency/BCP arrangements.
Major incident, service continuity and communications
The policy must require ITSM processes to integrate with business continuity, emergency management and crisis communications arrangements for disruptions affecting ICT services.
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure
The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
ITSM records often contain official information and must be handled according to classification and protective marking rules.
Medium - applies to incidents, changes, requests, knowledge and CMDB records.
The policy must require ICTSM records, knowledge articles, service catalogue entries and CMDB data to apply approved information handling, access and protective marking requirements.
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure
The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
Caveated information requires special handling in tickets, knowledge, CMDB items and supplier communications.
Medium - ITSM must enforce handling restrictions when such information is present.
Knowledge management, service desk and supplier communications
The policy must require caveated or specially handled information in ITSM tools or supplier workflows to be labelled, access-controlled and exchanged only through approved channels.
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure

The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
Service desk emails, notifications and supplier communications may carry OFFICIAL or classified information.
Medium - applies to email-based ITSM communications.
The policy must require service desk and ICTSM email communications to use approved protective markings and handling instructions when exchanging OFFICIAL or security classified information.
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure

The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
Security classification metadata supports access control, retrieval and records management in technology systems.
Medium - applies where ITSM platforms store or reference classified information.
Knowledge management, records and ITSM tool controls
The policy must require ITSM tools and repositories that store, process or reference classified information to capture and preserve required security classification and caveat metadata.
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure
Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
Rights metadata supports restrictions on use and disclosure of ITSM knowledge and records.
Medium - applies to knowledge and records where access restrictions are needed.
The policy must require restricted ITSM records and knowledge to capture rights, ownership and access limitation metadata where this is needed to control use, disclosure or retention.
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure
Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
Information holdings within ITSM tooling must be protected over their lifecycle according to sensitivity and business criticality.
High - applies to ITSM records, CMDB and knowledge repositories.
Knowledge management, CMDB and information lifecycle controls

The policy must require operational controls for ICTSM information holdings, including access, retention, review, archival and disposal controls aligned to information sensitivity and service criticality.
Records, knowledge, FOI, publication, retention and evidence management

OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
Tickets, knowledge, configuration records and service artefacts must be disposed of securely when retention obligations are met.
Medium - ITSM supports records retention and disposal.
The policy must require secure disposal of ICTSM records and information in accordance with authorised retention, records and information security requirements.
Records, knowledge, FOI, publication, retention and evidence management

Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
Classified ICTSM information requires approved destruction processes and evidence.
Low/Conditional - only where ITSM records or media contain classified information.
Knowledge management, CMDB and secure disposal
The policy must require classified information or media held in ITSM processes to be destroyed only through approved methods and recorded as evidence of completion.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
Service strategy, design, transition and operation must embed ISM cyber security principles across the full lifecycle.
High - direct technology lifecycle and service lifecycle requirement.
Service strategy, design, transition and operation
The policy must require ICT services to apply ISM-aligned security principles across planning, design, build, deployment, operation, maintenance and retirement.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
Risk-based ISM controls are a prerequisite for service design, acceptance and ongoing operation.
High - direct security control integration requirement.
Service design, transition and operational controls
The policy must require service owners to select, implement, evidence and review ISM controls on a risk basis before operational acceptance and during service operation.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management

The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
Systems must not enter operational service until residual security risks are accepted by an authorised officer.
High - direct service transition/operational acceptance requirement.
The policy must require operational acceptance criteria to include authorisation to operate, accepted residual risks, support readiness, monitoring, knowledge and CMDB completion before go-live.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
Change and reauthorisation decisions must be based on the ISM risk management approach.
The policy must require new services and material changes to assess security risk, update controls and obtain the required authorisation or reauthorisation before implementation.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
Service classification determines handling, monitoring, support, continuity and access requirements.
Configuration management, CMDB and service catalogue

The policy must require each ICT service and technology system to have its highest information classification and business criticality recorded in the CMDB/service catalogue and used to set controls and support requirements.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management

A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
A register of authorised systems aligns to the CMDB and service portfolio.

The policy must require the CMDB or authorised system register to record system owner, authorising officer, authorisation date, service owner, classification, residual risk decisions and lifecycle status.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management

Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
Significant functionality, architecture or security-environment changes must trigger reassessment and service risk review.

The policy must require significant changes, major releases, material incidents or security-environment changes to trigger reassessment of service authorisation, controls, support readiness and CMDB data.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
The TikTok application is prevented from being installed, and existing instances are removed, on government devices, unless a legitimate business reason exists.
Application deployment and request fulfilment controls must prevent prohibited applications on government devices.
Medium - ITSM supports endpoint/app request and deployment workflows.
Request fulfilment, release and deployment management

The policy must require application requests, packaging and deployment processes to enforce approved software lists, block prohibited applications and remove unauthorised installations through standard operational processes.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
The CSO or CISO approves any legitimate business reason for the use of the TikTok application on government devices and ensures specified mitigations are in place.
Exceptions for high-risk applications require business justification, approval and ongoing mitigations.
Medium - ITSM supports exception workflow and evidence.
Request fulfilment, change enablement and exception management

The policy must require exceptions for restricted applications to be raised through approved request/change workflows, endorsed by Security/CISO where required and tracked with mitigation, review and removal dates.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
Legacy IT creates service, security and continuity risk that must be visible in CMDB, problem and change processes.
High - direct legacy service risk requirement.
Configuration management, problem management and change enablement

The policy must require legacy services and unsupported components to be identified in the CMDB, risk assessed, monitored, patched or mitigated and managed through problem, change and roadmap processes.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
Technology assets and their components, classified as SECRET or below are stored in the appropriate Security Zone based on their aggregated security classification or business impact level.
Storage controls for technology assets affect configuration, asset custody and service continuity.
Low/Medium - physical security owns detail; ITSM records and interfaces apply.
Configuration management and asset custody interface
The policy must require configuration and asset records to identify storage, custody and classification requirements for technology assets and to interface with physical security procedures.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
Technology assets and their components classified as TOP SECRET are stored in suitable SCEC-endorsed racks or compartments within an accredited Security Zone Five area.
TOP SECRET asset storage controls are outside routine ITSM but must be recognised for affected services.
Conditional - only if NDIA services include TOP SECRET technology assets.
Configuration management and secure asset handling interface
The policy must require services with TOP SECRET assets to follow approved secure storage and handling procedures, with CMDB records and operational support restricted to authorised personnel.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance

Outsourced facilities that house technology assets and their components with a catastrophic business impact level are certified by ASIO T4 physical security and accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
Outsourced facilities hosting high-impact technology assets are a supplier and continuity dependency.
Medium - supplier management and service continuity interface.
The policy must require outsourced hosting/facility dependencies to be recorded, assured and reviewed as part of supplier governance, continuity planning and service risk management.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management
Technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the Information Security Manual.
Technology asset disposal affects service retirement, CMDB accuracy, data protection and evidence records.
Release, deployment, configuration and service retirement
The policy must require service retirement and asset disposal to include data sanitisation/destruction, CMDB updates, supplier obligations, evidence capture and closure approvals.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
Patch applications mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Patch application controls require coordinated change, release, testing and deployment management.
The policy must require application patching to be planned, prioritised by risk, tested, deployed, verified and reported through change and release processes aligned to Essential Eight targets.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
Patch operating systems mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Operating system patching is a core operational control that must be governed through change and release.
The policy must require operating system patches to be prioritised, scheduled, tested, deployed, verified and reported, with emergency change pathways for critical vulnerabilities.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
MFA changes affect access, request fulfilment, service desk support and user experience.
Medium - ITSM supports rollout, requests and incident handling.
Service desk, request fulfilment and change enablement
The policy must require MFA-related service changes, exceptions, incidents and access requests to be managed through approved workflows with Security oversight and user-impact communications.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Privileged access restrictions depend on controlled request, approval, review and incident processes.
High - direct service desk/request and operational control interface.
Request fulfilment, access requests and change enablement

The policy must require privileged access requests and changes to be approved, time-bound where appropriate, recorded, reviewed and removed when no longer required, with exceptions escalated to Security.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Application control depends on release/deployment and configuration controls for approved software.
High - direct release/deployment and CMDB requirement.
Release and deployment management; configuration management
The policy must require application allowlisting/control rules to be managed through change and release processes, aligned with the approved software catalogue and validated after deployment.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
Restrict Microsoft Office macros mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Macro restrictions affect application configuration, standard operating environments and exception requests.
Medium - ITSM supports deployment and exception management.
Change enablement, request fulfilment and SOE management
The policy must require macro-related configuration baselines, exceptions and changes to be governed through approved change/request workflows and periodically reviewed with Security.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
User application hardening mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
User application hardening requires managed configuration baselines and operational verification.
The policy must require user application hardening baselines to be deployed, verified and maintained through standard change, release and configuration management processes.
Service continuity, backup, resilience, critical services and emergency integration
Regular back-ups mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Backups are a service continuity dependency for restoration after disruptive incidents.
High - direct service continuity and DR interface requirement.
Service continuity, backup and disaster recovery interface
The policy must require critical services to have documented backup, restore and verification requirements, linked to DR plans, service criticality, RTO/RPO and regular restore testing.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration

The remaining mitigation strategies from the Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents are considered and, where required, implemented to achieve an acceptable level of residual risk for their entity.
Additional cyber mitigations may create ITSM controls, changes, monitoring requirements and service acceptance criteria.
Medium/High - applies through security uplift, change and operational controls.
Change enablement, service design and continual improvement

The policy must require cyber uplift actions and risk treatments that affect ICT services to be assessed, prioritised, implemented and evidenced through ITSM change, release, problem and service review processes.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
A Protective Domain Name System service or other security mechanisms is used to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints.
Protective DNS and related controls generate monitoring events and require service operations integration.
Medium - event monitoring and security operations interface.
Event monitoring, observability and incident management
The policy must require security monitoring events from PDNS or equivalent controls to be integrated with observability, alert triage, incident escalation and service reporting processes.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance
Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
Cloud supplier assurance affects service design, transition, acceptance and ongoing supplier management.
High - direct cloud supplier assurance requirement.

The policy must require cloud services to use suppliers with current required assurance (including IRAP where applicable) and to record assurance status in service acceptance and supplier governance artefacts.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance
Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
IRAP findings become service risks, remediation actions, changes or accepted residual risks.
High - direct service risk and change management requirement.
Supplier assurance, change enablement and risk acceptance

The policy must require IRAP findings and recommendations relevant to ICT services to be assessed, assigned, tracked through risk/change/problem processes and reviewed until closed or formally accepted.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance

Security classified or systems of government significance information and data is securely hosted using a Cloud Service Provider and Data Centre Provider that has been certified against the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
Hosting requirements affect service design, supplier selection, continuity and operational acceptance.
Conditional/High - applies to security classified or SOGS information and data.
Service design, supplier management and service continuity

The policy must require hosting decisions for security classified or SOGS services to satisfy relevant certification, data centre, continuity and operational acceptance requirements before production use.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance
The Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel is used when procuring certified data centre space and services.
Certified data centre procurement is a supplier management and service design control for hosting dependencies.
Medium - applies where NDIA procures certified data centre space/services.

The policy must require data centre dependencies and procurement pathways to be verified with procurement and security requirements, recorded in supplier/service records and reviewed during service lifecycle events.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance
Internet-connected technology systems, and the data they process, store or communicate, are protected by a gateway in accordance with the ISM and the Gateways Policy.
Not a separate current PSPF Release 2025 requirement; gateway control intent is covered by PSPF-214 and related gateway/SSE assurance requirements.
Not current - retain as superseded/reference only; do not include as a standalone obligation.

The policy should not cite PSPF-113 as a current standalone Release 2025 obligation; use current gateway or Secure Service Edge requirements, especially PSPF-214 and PSPF-114, when defining ITSM controls.
Cloud, hosting, gateway, data centre and infrastructure service assurance
Gateways or Secure Service Edges that have completed an IRAP assessment (or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways) against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
Gateway/SSE supplier assurance affects service design, operational acceptance and monitoring.
High - direct supplier and security service assurance requirement.
Supplier management, service design and observability

The policy must require gateways and Secure Service Edges used by ICT services to have required current assurance, be recorded as service dependencies and be monitored/reviewed through supplier and service governance.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
A vulnerability disclosure program and supporting processes and procedures are established to receive, verify, resolve and report on vulnerabilities disclosed by both internal and external sources.
Vulnerability disclosures must be converted into incidents, problems, changes and remediation evidence.
Vulnerability intake, incident, problem and change management

The policy must require vulnerability disclosures from internal or external sources to be received, triaged, risk assessed and managed through incident, problem and change workflows until remediation or risk acceptance.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
Access to supporting technology systems is fulfilled and supported through service desk and request workflows.
High - direct request fulfilment/access support requirement.
Service desk, request fulfilment and access requests

The policy must require access to ICT services, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications to be requested, approved, provisioned, changed and revoked through controlled service management processes.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID

A unique user identification, authentication and authorisation practice is implemented on each occasion where system access is granted, to manage access to systems holding security classified information.
Unique identification and authorisation controls require consistent access request and provisioning practices.
High - direct access request and service desk requirement.
Service desk, request fulfilment and access requests
The policy must require all system access requests to use unique user identification, approved authentication and authorisation practices, with evidence retained in the service management record.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
Approval for remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems in international locations is only granted if approved by the Australian Signals Directorate.
TOP SECRET remote access is outside routine ITSM but any ICT workflow must enforce approval and evidence.
Conditional - only where NDIA supports TOP SECRET systems or access.
Request fulfilment and security exception interface
The policy must require remote access requests for highly classified systems to be blocked unless approved through the required security authority and recorded with supporting risk/approval evidence.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions to allow personnel to work remotely in international locations.
International remote work decisions affect endpoint support, access, monitoring and service desk operations.
Medium/Conditional - HR/security own decision; ITSM controls access and support workflows.
Request fulfilment, service desk and remote access support

The policy must require ICT support for international remote work to occur only after the required security risk assessment and approval, with access, device, monitoring and support conditions recorded.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID

Personnel are not granted approval to work remotely in locations where Australian Government information or resources are exposed to extrajudicial directions from a foreign government that conflict with Australian law, unless operationally required.
Remote work in higher-risk locations may require blocking or tailored access controls.
Medium/Conditional - ITSM implements access changes after security decision.
Request fulfilment, access control and exception management

The policy must require service desk and access management processes to enforce approved remote work restrictions, including blocking, suspending or tailoring access where Security identifies unacceptable location risk.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
The CSO, CISO (or other relevant security practitioner) is advised prior to separation or transfer of any proposed cessation of employment resulting from misconduct or other adverse reasons.
Adverse separation or transfer events require rapid security notification and coordinated access actions.
Medium - HR/Security own trigger; ITSM supports notification and access workflows.
Service desk operation and offboarding interface

The policy must require ICT service desk/offboarding processes to escalate adverse separation or transfer notifications to Security/CISO and initiate priority access review or suspension where directed.
Access, identity, privileged access, remote access, offboarding and Digital ID
Separating personnel have their access to Australian Government resources withdrawn upon separation or transfer from the entity.
Access removal is a critical request fulfilment and service desk control for separating or transferring personnel.
High - direct service desk/request fulfilment requirement.
Service desk, request fulfilment and access revocation

The policy must require timely withdrawal, suspension or transfer of access to ICT systems, resources and service roles when personnel separate or change roles, with evidence retained in service records.
Change, release, configuration, asset, transition and retirement management

A Technology Asset Stocktake and Technology Security Risk Management Plan is created to identify and manage the entity's internet-facing systems or services to ensure continuous visibility and monitoring of the entity's resource and technology estate.
A technology asset stocktake and TSRMP require accurate CMDB, dependency mapping and monitoring coverage.
High - direct CMDB, observability and service portfolio requirement.

The policy must require the CMDB/service portfolio to maintain accurate technology asset, service, dependency, internet-facing status and monitoring data to support the Technology Security Risk Management Plan.
Cyber controls, patching, vulnerability, hardening and secure configuration
Approved post-quantum cryptographic encryption algorithms are used for newly procured cryptographic equipment and software in accordance with the ISM's guidelines for cryptography.
Post-quantum cryptography requirements affect procurement, service design, change and release of cryptographic technologies.
Medium - applies to new cryptographic equipment/software and supplier solutions.
